_comment: Cross-language contract for the SSO callback's error-code vocabulary (#3951).
The backend (packages/api/src/trueppm_api/apps/sso/services.py's OIDCError
hierarchy, plus the literal `error="..."` codes in sso/views.py) and the
frontend (SsoCompletePage.tsx's ERROR_COPY) each independently enumerate the
same set of SSO callback error codes, and nothing kept them in sync — the file's
own comment records four codes that silently degraded to generic copy for
months (#2876) before anyone noticed. This file is the third artifact both
sides assert against: a pytest for the derived backend set, a vitest for the
web's authored ERROR_COPY keys. Drift on either side fails a pipeline instead
of surviving a code review.
`mapped` is every code that gets its own actionable ERROR_COPY entry.
`genericFallback` is the closed set of codes that intentionally fall back to
the generic 'Something went wrong' copy — today just `oidc_error`, the
OIDCError base-class default. It is not currently reachable (every subclass
overrides `code`, and nothing raises the base class directly), but it exists
as the safety net for a future subclass that forgets to. There is no more
specific copy to give a code that by definition carries no information beyond
'something in the OIDC flow failed', so this is a stated choice, not an
oversight — see the comment beside ERROR_COPY in SsoCompletePage.tsx.
Adding a new backend error code: give the raising class (or view redirect) a
distinct `code`, then decide whether it gets real copy (add it to `mapped`
here AND to ERROR_COPY in SsoCompletePage.tsx) or is an intentional generic
fallback (add it to `genericFallback` here). Either alone fails the gate.
